title: August and the Ledger
premise: Retired detective Ulyana Sandoval has traded homicide files for a failing bookshop in the river town of August, but when a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from Ulyana's own closet, his quiet exile ends. The victim clutched a page from an old merchant's ledger — a coded record of bribes paid by August's founding families to bury a decades-old wrongful conviction. As Ulyana decodes the ledger with help from a sharp-eyed archivist named Wren, he realizes the killer is someone inside the circle preparing the town's anniversary dinner, silencing anyone who might expose the original crime. In the end, Ulyana exposes the truth at the anniversary toast itself, choosing justice outside the law over the badge he no longer wears, and finds belonging at last in the town he'd only ever observed.
about_author: Silas Hartwell is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent fifteen years covering courtrooms and county fairs before turning to fiction. He lives above a secondhand bookshop and writes mysteries about places that remember too much.

chapters.title: Watermarks
chapters.summary: Ulyana Sandoval opens the bookshop on a gray morning, counting unsold stock and regretting his retirement. A police cruiser idles outside; an old colleague, Detective Marsh, asks him to look at something unofficial. POV: Ulyana. Beat: restless unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man Wore My Coat
chapters.summary: At the river landing, Ulyana identifies the body's clothing as his own — items stolen from his shop's donation bin. The dead man is unknown to him, pockets holding one torn ledger page. POV: Ulyana. Beat: violation and vertigo; the case has chosen him.

chapters.title: Inventory of Strangers
chapters.summary: Back at the shop, Ulyana reconstructs which books are missing alongside the clothes, finding a hollowed-out volume used as a hiding place. Someone was using his shop as a dead drop. POV: Ulyana. Beat: paranoia blooming in familiar rooms.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor, a young town archivist and regular customer, recognizes the ledger page's paper stock as pre-war stationery from the Hollis Mercantile. She offers her help; Ulyana hesitates, then accepts. POV: alternating Ulyana/Wren. Beat: first spark of trust and alliance.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: August prepares its sesquicentennial dinner. Ulyana attends a committee meeting and watches the founding families — the Ashcombes, Vances, and Mayor Dell — rehearse their polished history. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the sense of a stage being set.

chapters.title: Ledger Logic
chapters.summary: Wren and Ulyana discover the ledger uses a double-entry code: legitimate sales figures conceal payments listed under false names. The first decoded entry implicates a bribe dated forty years ago. POV: Wren. Beat: intellectual thrill curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Conviction Called Closed
chapters.summary: The coded payment matches the 1985 conviction of Elias Boone, a dockworker hanged for a fire that killed three people. Ulyana remembers the case from his academy days as the town's tidy tragedy. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief for a man already failed once.

chapters.title: The Widow's Doorstep
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Corinne Boone, Elias's elderly daughter, who slams the door — then reopens it and says only: 'You're late by forty years.' POV: Ulyana. Beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Marsh's Warning
chapters.summary: Detective Marsh privately warns Ulyana off: the case touches families who fund the police pension. He offers a choice — stay retired or become a target. POV: Marsh. Beat: loyalty tested; duty pulling against friendship.

chapters.title: Second Entry
chapters.summary: Decoding continues: a second payment, made annually for decades, is labeled 'maintenance.' Someone has been paying to keep the Boone verdict buried. POV: Wren. Beat: cold clarity — this is ongoing, not historical.

chapters.title: The Missing Apprentice
chapters.summary: The drowned man is identified as Tobias Finch, a former clerk at the county records office who had been quietly copying the ledger. His landlady says he vanished two weeks ago. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the victim becomes a person; stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: Hollowed Spines
chapters.summary: Ulyana searches his own shelves and finds three more hollowed books, each holding ledger fragments — meaning the drop ran through his shop for years without his knowledge. POV: Ulyana. Beat: betrayal by proximity; his sanctuary was never clean.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: Mayor Dell invites Ulyana personally to the anniversary dinner, a courtesy that feels like a leash. At the event hall, Ulyana notes the seating chart mirrors the ledger's family initials. POV: Ulyana. Beat: menace dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Confession That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Matriarch Vivian Ashcombe corners Ulyana, hinting she knows about the ledger and urging him to let 'sleeping towns lie' — while slipping him a key to a storage unit. POV: Ulyana. Beat: ambiguous ally or bait?

chapters.title: Unit 12
chapters.summary: The storage unit holds boxes of county records and a complete copy of the ledger's missing middle section — plus evidence someone else visited recently: fresh cigarette ash, a turned lock. POV: Wren. Beat: racing the killer to the same prize.

chapters.title: Fire Remembered
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: through Corinne's telling, the 1985 warehouse fire is reconstructed — Elias was framed because he refused to falsify shipping manifests for smuggled goods. POV: Corinne. Beat: the past rendered vivid and unforgivable.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Leaving the storage unit, Wren and Ulyana are followed through the river district. They lose the car but find a dropped glove monogrammed with the Vance family crest. POV: Ulyana. Beat: pursuit adrenaline; the enemy has a name.

chapters.title: Deputy Vance
chapters.summary: Deputy Raymond Vance claims innocence when confronted, but his alibi for the night Tobias died is thin. Marsh quietly confirms Vance was seen near the river. POV: Marsh. Beat: law enforcement splintering along old loyalties.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Stakeout
chapters.summary: Ulyana baits the trap: he publicly restocks the hollowed books, hoping whoever maintained the drop will return. All night he waits among his own inventory. POV: Ulyana. Beat: patience as suspense; the hunter becomes the lure.

chapters.title: Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Someone enters at 3 a.m. — not Vance but a nervous young woman, Priya, who confesses she was paid to maintain the drop by 'a committee man' and fears for her life. POV: Ulyana. Beat: relief complicated by new danger.

chapters.title: Priya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya reveals the final pages: the last entry, dated this spring, reads 'settlement — B.C., final.' Whoever 'B.C.' is just made the last payment before exposure. POV: Wren. Beat: the net tightening around an unnamed center.

chapters.title: Corinne Opens the Door Again
chapters.summary: Corinne shares Elias's letters, including one naming his accuser by initial: B.C. Ulyana realizes the initials match Bartholomew Crane, the beloved retired judge hosting the anniversary dinner. POV: Ulyana. Beat: horror — the villain is the town's conscience.

chapters.title: Judge Crane's Toast Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ulyana attends a public rehearsal where Judge Crane practices his anniversary toast about 'a town that forgives itself.' Their eyes meet; Crane smiles warmly. POV: Ulyana. Beat: dread wrapped in civility.

chapters.title: Marsh Crosses the Line
chapters.summary: Marsh gives Ulyana the case file on the 1985 fire, officially sealed, knowing it may end his career. 'I can't do it in uniform,' he says. POV: Marsh. Beat: sacrifice; duty realigned with justice.

chapters.title: Priya Disappears
chapters.summary: Priya vanishes after agreeing to testify. Her apartment is scrubbed clean; a single hollowed book sits on her shelf, empty. POV: Ulyana. Beat: guilt and urgency — silence is spreading.

chapters.title: The River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Tobias's full notebook surfaces downstream, waterproofed, containing his reconstruction of the smuggling route and a note naming Crane directly. POV: Wren. Beat: the dead man testifies at last.

chapters.title: Vance's Choice
chapters.summary: Deputy Vance, confronted with the glove and the file, breaks: he protected Crane out of family debt, not belief. He agrees to give a statement after the anniversary — a delay Ulyana distrusts. POV: Vance. Beat: cowardice cracking toward courage.

chapters.title: What the Shop Is Worth
chapters.summary: An anonymous buyer offers Ulyana triple value for the bookshop — clearly an attempt to remove him from town before the dinner. He refuses. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the shop becomes a stand-in for belonging itself.

chapters.title: Wren's Discovery
chapters.summary: Wren finds the ledger's true key hidden in the mercantile's founding charter: entries map to pew numbers in the First Church, where physical proof — the original manifests — were cached. POV: Wren. Beat: triumph shadowed by fear of what the proof will cost.

chapters.title: Church Basement
chapters.summary: Behind a loose pew panel, Ulyana recovers the manifests proving Crane falsified the fire investigation. As he leaves, the church lights snap on: Judge Crane is waiting. POV: Ulyana. Beat: confrontation deferred by courtesy — two men speaking in pleasantries with knives underneath.

chapters.title: Tea with the Judge
chapters.summary: Crane offers Ulyana a place in history: destroy the manifests and be remembered as the detective who kept August whole. Ulyana refuses; Crane promises, gently, that the dinner will proceed regardless. POV: Ulyana. Beat: love against duty inverted — Crane loves the town into lying.

chapters.title: Marsh Is Suspended
chapters.summary: Crane's allies move first: Marsh is suspended on fabricated misconduct charges, cutting Ulyana off from official protection. POV: Marsh. Beat: isolation deepens; the law itself is the obstacle.

chapters.title: Corinne Decides
chapters.summary: Corinne agrees to attend the anniversary dinner — the first Boone to enter that hall since the hanging — and to stand when Ulyana calls her father's name. POV: Corinne. Beat: quiet, devastating resolve.

chapters.title: Setting the Table
chapters.summary: The day before the dinner, Ulyana and Wren plan the exposure: copies of the evidence distributed to press and state police timed to the toast, so no one can un-ring the bell. POV: Wren. Beat: tension of choreography; everything must land at once.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Eve of the anniversary: Priya's body is found in the river, dressed — like Tobias — in borrowed clothes, this time from Corinne's closet. The message is unmistakable. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief weaponized; the killer is taunting them.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The hall glitters. Crane begins his toast to 'forgiveness.' Ulyana stands, names Elias Boone, and reads the first manifest line aloud as Corinne rises beside him. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the held breath of a town.

chapters.title: What Crane Did Next
chapters.summary: Crane calmly denies everything — until Vance walks in, in uniform despite suspension, and places his sworn statement on the head table. Crane's composure fractures; he reaches for the podium as if it were a gavel. POV: Vance. Beat: the turn; cowardice completing its arc.

chapters.title: After the Toast
chapters.summary: State police, tipped by the timed packets, arrest Crane in front of the town he curated for forty years. Some applaud; some weep; some leave early. POV: Ulyana. Beat: justice arriving imperfect, public, and real.

chapters.title: Reopening the Case
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Elias Boone's conviction is vacated. Marsh is reinstated; Priya and Tobias are mourned properly, their names read into the record. POV: Wren. Beat: mourning braided with repair.

chapters.title: August, Again
chapters.summary: Ulyana restocks the shop, fills the hollowed books with wildflowers instead of secrets, and hangs a photo of Corinne at the counter. Wren stays for coffee after closing. The town finally includes him. POV: Ulyana. Beat: belonging earned, love begun, the ledger closed.
